cases.description: Microsoft's first documented example, at the six decimals it publishes
cases.expected_note: Microsoft publishes =SQRTPI(1) = 1.772454 ("Square root of pi"). DERIVATION: sqrt(1*pi) = 1.772453850905516027298 at 50 digits, which is 1.772454 at the published precision. Microsoft's page was read live on 2026-08-31 at https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/functions/sqrtpi-function. FETCH NOTE FOR THIS BATCH: batch F recorded every /en-us/office/<name>-function-<guid> URL returning Microsoft's 'Sorry, the page you're looking for can't be found' body; today BOTH paths serve the article again -- the GUID form redirects to /en-us/excel/functions/<slug>-function -- and every page cited in this batch came back complete (217-223 KB) in one or two attempts, with no 87 KB stub responses. Nothing here is sourced from a search snippet or a mirror.

Microsoft publishes =SQRTPI(2) = 2.506628 ("Square root of 2 * pi"). Derived independently as sqrt(2*pi) = 2.506628274631000502416, i.e. 2.506628 at the published precision. This is also the normal distribution's normalising constant, so the digits are checkable against any statistics reference.

cases.description: The same example carried to ten decimals
cases.expected_note: Asserted at ten places from the derivation: 2.5066282746. Six published decimals cannot see an engine that multiplies before or after taking the root in a way that loses a bit.

cases.description: Zero, which is inside the documented range
cases.expected_note: The only Remark on the page is "If number < 0, SQRTPI returns the #NUM! error value", so zero is inside the documented range and sqrt(0*pi) = 0 exactly.

cases.description: A structural round trip: squaring the result and dividing by pi must give back the argument
cases.expected_note: SQRTPI(n)^2 / PI() = n exactly in real arithmetic, for any n. A structural assertion with no derived constant, and it is sharp about the ARGUMENT handling: an engine that computed sqrt(pi)*n, or sqrt(n)+pi, or sqrt(n/pi) would pass none of it.

cases.description: A negative argument, which the page excludes
cases.expected_note: The page's single Remark publishes: "If number < 0, SQRTPI returns the #NUM! error value."
